messages.content: Back from Oregon and I need to open the last fall loop: Front Range, Sunday Nov. 3 through Thursday Nov. 7. Anchors are Monday 7:50 a.m. counselor breakfast in Fort Collins, Monday night college fair in Boulder, Tuesday school visits in Westminster and Lakewood, Wednesday afternoon transfer table in Colorado Springs, and Thursday morning counselor coffee near Denver Tech Center. Can you compare flying into Denver with a rental car versus just driving from Salt Lake? I also need a sensible route order and hotel zones with early breakfast and practical dinner access before I put refundable holds on rooms.

Absolutely. I’d treat this as a reliability question more than a pure cost question. Two quick checks before I rank it: if you fly Sunday, can you leave SLC after lunch or early afternoon, and is the rental car reimbursable if it saves a weather drive? Also, do you need to be home Thursday for anything that would make a later afternoon return a problem?

I can leave after lunch Sunday. Rental car is reimbursable as long as I keep the itemized receipt and note why I didn’t drive. I don’t need to be home Thursday until dinner-ish. My hesitation on driving is early snow on I-80 and being wrecked before that 7:50 breakfast.

Then the cleaner plan is fly plus rental unless the fares are unreasonable. Flight plus rental gives you a short Sunday travel day, enough daylight to get from DEN to Fort Collins, and far less exposure to I-80 weather; the downsides are rental cost, airport pickup time, parking, and possible tolls. Driving avoids airfare and uses your own car, but it puts 8-plus hours on both ends of the trip and makes Monday morning fragile. Because the first commitment is early in Fort Collins, I would not make the Sunday drive unless the forecast is dry and you can leave Salt Lake very early.
If flying, should Sunday night be Fort Collins itself or Loveland? The breakfast is near CSU.

Fort Collins. Loveland is fine on price, but it adds 25 to 35 minutes on the morning you most need predictability. I’d look near CSU or Old Town if rates are reasonable, or Fort Collins south/Harmony if you want easier I-25 access and chain hotels. For the hold, verify breakfast starts by 6:30 or plan a coffee-and-grab backup. Dinner is easier around Old Town or Harmony than by the interstate after 9.
Map the route order assuming I land at DEN Sunday afternoon.

Route shape: Sunday land DEN, pick up the car, and drive straight to Fort Collins before dark. Monday do the 7:50 breakfast, use mid-day for follow-ups or a school stop, drive to Boulder for the evening fair, and sleep somewhere between Boulder and Tuesday’s first school. Tuesday do Westminster and Lakewood, then decide whether to push south that evening. Wednesday be in Colorado Springs for the afternoon transfer table. Wednesday night should probably be DTC or nearby, not Colorado Springs, because Thursday morning is at DTC and you’ll want a simple airport return after.
The Monday night piece is the one I can’t see clearly. Boulder rooms look high. What about Broomfield, Westminster, or Denver West?

My ranking right now: first, Broomfield/Interlocken or Superior, because it is the easiest after the Boulder fair, has lots of dinner options around FlatIron Crossing, and is still workable for Westminster or Lakewood. Second, Westminster, which is good if the Westminster school is first and parking is usually easier, but food can be more scattered depending on the hotel. Third, Denver West or Golden, which is best only if Lakewood is the first Tuesday visit; it makes the late post-fair drive longer. Boulder is worth it only if the fair ends very late or weather is bad.
For Tuesday night, I don’t want to be penny-wise and dumb. Wednesday table is afternoon, not morning, and Thursday coffee is DTC at 8:30.

With an afternoon Colorado Springs table, you have flexibility. If Tuesday visits end by mid-afternoon and the roads are dry, sleeping in Colorado Springs Tuesday is comfortable: you arrive, eat, and have a calm Wednesday morning. If Tuesday runs late or Monument Hill looks icy, sleep north of it, either Castle Rock, DTC, or Denver south, and drive down Wednesday late morning. Wednesday night I’d sleep DTC regardless, because driving up from Colorado Springs before an 8:30 coffee is the fragile move.
Can you give me the hotel zones to hold? I’m not booking tonight, just refundable holds.

Hold one per zone: Sunday Fort Collins near CSU/Old Town if price is okay, otherwise Harmony Road/I-25; Monday Broomfield/Interlocken as first choice, Westminster as backup, and Denver West only if Tuesday starts in Lakewood; Tuesday Colorado Springs north or central if you can arrive before dinner, with Castle Rock or DTC as the weather backup; Wednesday DTC/Greenwood Village near I-25 or Belleview. For each hold, check breakfast start time, free versus paid parking, itemized folio availability, and whether there is a restaurant within a 10-minute walk or a reliable late pickup option.
The fair in Boulder is scheduled to end at 8:15 right now. If I stay Broomfield, am I okay for dinner after?

Yes, Broomfield/Interlocken is one of the safer meal choices after that. FlatIron Crossing and the US-36 corridor have more options than a random Westminster business park, though some kitchens will be closing by 9:30. I’d still eat something before the fair if possible, then use Broomfield for a lighter late dinner or pickup. If you hold Denver West, late dinner gets thinner unless you go out of your way.
What about rental car class and parking? I don’t want a giant SUV if I don’t need one.

Book a compact or midsize SUV only if the price difference is modest; otherwise a standard sedan is fine for normal Front Range roads. AWD is not guaranteed unless the rental class says so, so don’t overpay thinking it solves everything. For reimbursement, keep the rental agreement, final receipt, fuel receipt, hotel parking lines, and any toll charges. Also check whether the hotel lots are surface and free; downtown Boulder and Fort Collins parking are where surprises are more likely.
Thursday return: the DTC coffee should end about 10:15. Is a midday flight okay, or should I go later afternoon?

A true midday flight is too tight if you are returning a rental at DEN. From DTC to the airport can be 35 to 60 minutes, then fuel, rental return, shuttle or walk, security, and weather slack. I’d target a nonstop departing roughly 2:30 to 4:30 p.m. Anything around noon would require leaving the coffee early. After 5 p.m. is safe but wastes the afternoon unless the fare is much better.
Good. Look for Sunday afternoon outbound and Thursday midafternoon nonstop. If seat maps are open, I’d like a window again, but that can wait.

Plan for holds tonight: fly SLC-DEN Sunday afternoon and rent at DEN; sleep Fort Collins Sunday, Broomfield/Interlocken Monday with Westminster as backup, Colorado Springs Tuesday only if the weather and Tuesday end time cooperate, and DTC Wednesday. Driving from Salt Lake stays a backup only if the forecast clears and fares jump. Before placing holds, verify 6:00 to 6:30 breakfast starts for the early mornings, parking charges, cancellation cutoff, late-food options, and itemized folios. For flights, shortlist nonstop Sunday after lunch and Thursday 2:30 to 4:30 p.m.; request window seats wherever the seat map lets you.

messages.content: Front Range details changed before I book. Boulder fair now ends at 8:35, Lakewood moved to 7:30 Tuesday morning, Westminster is later that morning, and the Colorado Springs transfer table is confirmed from 2:00 to 5:15 Wednesday. Boulder and Denver West rooms are tightening because of a campus weekend. Colorado Springs has cheaper parking, but fewer late dinner options near the venue. Can you rerank the hotel sequence?

Yes. The Lakewood 7:30 start pulls Monday night west or south, while the 8:35 Boulder ending argues against a long post-fair drive. Before I lock the ranking: would you rather keep the post-fair drive under about 20 minutes and wake earlier Tuesday, or drive farther Monday night to make Tuesday morning easier?
Keep the post-fair drive reasonable. I can wake early Tuesday if breakfast is available by 6.

Then Broomfield/Interlocken stays first for Monday night. It keeps the Boulder-to-hotel drive short and still lets you reach Lakewood if you leave around 6:30 or 6:35. Westminster is second, mostly as a rate backup. Denver West is third now: it helps the 7:30 Lakewood visit, but after an 8:35 fair it makes the late drive longer than I’d want unless the Broomfield breakfast fails. Boulder is not worth the price unless weather is ugly.
Which exact checks do I need for the Broomfield hold? It shows breakfast but not the start time.

Call or message the property and ask four things: does weekday breakfast start at 6:00, is parking free or paid, will the folio separate room/tax/parking, and what is the actual cancellation cutoff for the Monday night stay. Also ask what food is realistic after 9:15 p.m.; ideally there is a hotel pantry plus something near FlatIron Crossing or a reliable pickup spot. If breakfast starts at 6:30 instead of 6:00, you can still make Lakewood, but it becomes grab-and-go only.
For Tuesday night, does Colorado Springs still make sense with the 2:00 table?

Yes, if you can leave the Denver-area visit by about 3:30 to 4:00 Tuesday and Monument Hill looks normal. That gets you into Colorado Springs early enough to eat and makes Wednesday calm. If Tuesday runs past 4:30 or there is snow/ice on I-25, keep a north-side option instead, preferably DTC or Castle Rock, and drive down Wednesday late morning. Because the table ends at 5:15, Wednesday night should be DTC.
The Colorado Springs hotel closest to the venue has free parking but maybe no restaurant. Is that a problem?

Not if you arrive Tuesday before 7. It becomes a problem only if the day slips late. Verify three meal items there: one dinner option within a 10-minute drive, delivery that actually reaches the hotel, and a market or snack shelf in the lobby. Breakfast is less critical Wednesday because your table starts at 2, but still confirm the start time for reimbursement notes. Also verify the cancellation cutoff, ideally Monday Nov. 4 or Tuesday Nov. 5 rather than earlier.
What sequence would you hold tonight, including backups?

Hold this sequence: Sunday Fort Collins near Harmony or CSU; Monday Broomfield/Interlocken primary, Westminster backup only until breakfast and parking are confirmed; Tuesday Colorado Springs north/central primary, with DTC or Castle Rock as the weather backup if it is fully refundable; Wednesday DTC/Greenwood Village primary. I would release Denver West unless Broomfield breakfast starts after 6:30 or the Broomfield rate jumps.
Can you put it in a verification list so I can call three properties quickly?

Call list: Fort Collins Sunday: breakfast by 6:30, Sunday dinner nearby after arrival, free parking, itemized folio, and cancellation cutoff for Nov. 3. Broomfield Monday: breakfast must start at 6:00 or have reliable grab-and-go, parking/free lot, late food after 9 p.m., itemized folio, and whether cancellation is due Nov. 3 or Nov. 4. Colorado Springs Tuesday: free parking, dinner/delivery if arrival slips, cancellation through Nov. 4 or Nov. 5, breakfast time, and folio. DTC Wednesday: breakfast by 6:30, paid parking clearly itemized if not free, easy dinner after the drive from Colorado Springs, and cancellation cutoff for Nov. 6. Ranking remains Broomfield over Westminster for Monday, Colorado Springs Tuesday only if weather stays ordinary, and DTC Wednesday for the 8:30 coffee.

messages.content: Airfare is finally workable. Need the final decision tonight before the room holds expire. I see a Sunday SLC-DEN nonstop around 3 and Thursday returns either 11:55 cheaper or 3:35. Snow is now in the I-80 forecast, so driving feels like a bad idea. Can you help finalize flights, rental car, and hotels?

Yes. With I-80 snow in the forecast and a 7:50 Monday breakfast in Fort Collins, I’d choose flight plus rental and drop the drive plan. The 11:55 Thursday return cuts the DTC coffee too close; the 3:35 return is the safer choice. Which carriers and fares are you seeing? If the price difference is small, schedule and ticket flexibility should win.

Delta is $28 more than United on the outbound and about the same on the return, and I’d rather avoid basic economy. Sunday Delta Main leaves SLC at 3:10 and lands DEN at 4:37. Thursday Delta Main leaves DEN at 3:35 and lands SLC at 5:12. United is similar but lands a little later Thursday.

Take Delta Main Cabin if the $28 difference is reimbursable. The schedule is clean, and avoiding basic economy is worth it for this trip. DEN arrival at 4:37 gives enough time for rental pickup and the drive to Fort Collins before full dark. Thursday 3:35 gives space for the DTC coffee, fuel, rental return, and security. Request window seats now if the seat map is open; otherwise set a check-in reminder.
Rental car: Avis standard sedan is cheapest, midsize SUV is $44 more total. Snow is mostly west of Laramie, not Denver, but I could see slick spots.

I’d pick the midsize SUV for $44 more if it remains reimbursable; it gives slightly better clearance and comfort without being oversized. Don’t assume AWD unless Avis lists it. Set pickup at DEN for about 5:15 p.m. Sunday and return by 1:30 p.m. Thursday. Decline prepaid fuel unless the rate is unusually favorable; fuel it yourself before the airport and keep the receipt.

Hotels I have on hold: Hampton Fort Collins Harmony Sunday, Homewood Broomfield Monday, Hyatt Place Colorado Springs/Garden of the Gods Tuesday, and Hampton DTC Wednesday. Cancellation language says Fort Collins by 6 p.m. Nov. 2, Broomfield by 11:59 p.m. Nov. 3, Colorado Springs by 6 p.m. Nov. 4, and DTC by 6 p.m. Nov. 5. Parking looks free except DTC is $12.

That sequence works. Keep Fort Collins Sunday; keep Broomfield Monday because the Boulder fair ends at 8:35 and Lakewood at 7:30 is manageable with an early departure; keep Colorado Springs Tuesday if you can leave the Denver-area visit by about 3:30 to 4:00 and Monument Hill looks okay; keep DTC Wednesday for the 8:30 coffee and airport return. Make sure the DTC parking charge appears on the folio.
Should I hold a DTC backup for Tuesday too, or is that overkill?

Hold it only if it is fully refundable past Monday and not prepaid. It is a useful weather backup: if Tuesday runs late or I-25 over Monument Hill looks bad, sleep DTC Tuesday and drive to Colorado Springs Wednesday late morning. If adding it creates another cancellation deadline tonight, skip it and use the Colorado Springs plan.
Room types: I’m solo, so one queen or king is fine. I don’t want a double-double unless that’s all that’s left.

Book single-bed rooms where selectable: queen or king is fine. Avoid double/double unless it is the only refundable option. On each confirmation, save the room type, room rate, taxes, parking line if any, and the cancellation timestamp.
Give me the final booking summary with last safe cancellation dates and receipt items. Then I’ll buy it.

Final choice: fly, do not drive. Book Delta Main Cabin SLC-DEN Sun Nov. 3, 3:10 p.m.-4:37 p.m.; Delta Main Cabin DEN-SLC Thu Nov. 7, 3:35 p.m.-5:12 p.m. Request window seats on both legs or set a reminder for check-in. Avis DEN pickup about 5:15 p.m. Sunday, return by 1:30 p.m. Thursday; midsize SUV if the $44 increase is reimbursable, otherwise standard sedan. Hotels: Hampton Fort Collins Harmony Sunday, cancel by 6 p.m. Nov. 2; Homewood Broomfield Monday, cancel by 11:59 p.m. Nov. 3; Hyatt Place Colorado Springs/Garden of the Gods Tuesday, cancel by 6 p.m. Nov. 4; Hampton DTC Wednesday, cancel by 6 p.m. Nov. 5, with $12 parking itemized. Verify breakfast hours on Fort Collins, Broomfield, and DTC; Colorado Springs dinner backup matters more than breakfast. Save airfare receipt, e-ticket, Avis agreement and final receipt, fuel receipt, hotel folios, parking, tolls, and a screenshot or note of the I-80 snow forecast for the reimbursement file.
